summary: Gave node1 (SONiC) routed addresses on both its data-plane segments (eth1=172.20.1.1/24 toward node2, eth2=172.20.2.1/24 toward node3), enabled IPv4 forwarding, and added corresponding static routes on node2 and node3 (each pointing to node1 as gateway for the other's subnet). Verified working node2<->node3 path via node1 (ttl=63, one hop). Made the config persist by writing eth1/eth2 static addressing into /etc/network/interfaces.d/datalinks (sourced by SONiC's networking.service, untouched by the interfaces-config.service reconciler that only rewrites the main file for eth0) plus /etc/sysctl.d/99-antrieb.conf for forwarding, and by creating persistent NetworkManager connection profiles + static routes on node2/node3. Ran the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes: captured boot_id + health baseline, issued native reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, and confirmed recovered config/connectivity. All three nodes came back with the config auto-restored and node2<->node3 reachability fully working (0% packet loss) after each restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (SONiC/Debian) interfaces: found eth1/eth2 as unaddressed data-plane NICs toward node2/node3, eth0 as DHCP management
Inspected node2/node3 (RHEL7): found eth0 management (DHCP) and eth1 unaddressed data-plane NIC
Confirmed SONiC config CLI rejects non-Ethernet* interface names, ruling out configdb-based persistence for eth1/eth2
Confirmed interfaces-config.service only templates the main /etc/network/interfaces (eth0/lo) and sources /etc/network/interfaces.d/*, making that directory safe for persistent eth1/eth2 config
Wrote /etc/network/interfaces.d/datalinks on node1 with static addresses 172.20.1.1/24 (eth1) and 172.20.2.1/24 (eth2); applied live via ifup
Wrote /etc/sysctl.d/99-antrieb.conf on node1 enabling ip_forward and per-interface forwarding on eth1/eth2; applied live via sysctl -p

Created persistent NetworkManager connection 'eth1' on node2 (172.20.1.2/24, static route 172.20.2.0/24 via 172.20.1.1) and on node3 (172.20.2.2/24, static route 172.20.1.0/24 via 172.20.2.1) via sudo nmcli
Verified node2<->node3 ping success routed through node1 (ttl=63)
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health baseline on all three nodes

Restarted node1 via native `reboot`, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed, verified eth1/eth2 addresses, forwarding sysctls, and SONiC containers recovered, and re-verified node2<->node3 connectivity (0% loss)

Restarted node2 via native `sudo reboot`, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed, verified eth1 IP/route recovered via NetworkManager persistence, and re-verified connectivity to node3 (0% loss)

Restarted node3 via native `sudo reboot`, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed, verified eth1 IP/route recovered via NetworkManager persistence, and re-verified connectivity to node2 (0% loss)
